title: Internal docs: align reliability language with tiered SLOs + link error budget runbooks
author: Elliot Price
description: Summary: This updates internal docs to match the tiered SLO + error budget program language and to make it easier for oncall/support/PMs to reference the canonical definitions and response runbooks. This is not changing any commercial SLA wording; it is aligning how we talk about reliability (and what we measure) across Hosted API vs Dedicated. Motivation / background: We’ve had repeated confusion in escalations (SUP-3950, SUP-3972) where customers referenced their own probes while we referenced internal dashboards with different exclusions. In parallel, SRE is publishing tiered SLOs + error budget policy; our internal docs had older “availability target” statements that were ambiguous (and in some cases implied guarantees outside the defined SLO scope). What changed (high level): (1) Added a single internal landing page for reliability language and references ("Reliability: tiers, SLOs, and error budgets") with links to the canonical Confluence pages for SLO definitions, SLI specs, and policy enforcement. (2) Updated Hosted API docs to explicitly say "SLOs are tier-specific" and to reference the correct SLIs (success/5xx/timeout, streaming disconnect rate, and latency SLIs including TTFT vs total stream duration). (3) Updated Dedicated docs to include pool readiness as a first-class indicator and to clarify how Dedicated isolation affects expectations during regional or upstream incidents (including when fallbacks may/ may not be used). (4) Added runbook links to the error-budget exhaustion response checklist and comms guidelines; included a short “What to do when the budget is burning” section intended for non-SRE readers (Support/CS, PM). (5) Replaced a few ambiguous phrases like “five nines” / “always available” with the approved tier-aware phrasing ("measured over rolling 28 days, with documented exclusions"). Notes on wording decisions: - Kept all customer-facing language explicitly non-contractual and pointed to the canonical internal SLO pages; this PR does not publish a new public SLA. - Wherever we mention availability, we include: tier (Hosted vs Dedicated), measurement window, primary SLI name, and a link to exclusions (customer-side timeouts, invalid auth, misuse). - For streaming endpoints, we now consistently distinguish: TTFT latency vs end-to-end stream duration vs disconnect rate; the previous docs conflated these and caused confusion when debugging "slow" reports. Reviewer checklist: - SRE: confirm wording matches tiered SLO definitions + error budget policy, and that we’re not implying enforcement behavior that isn’t shipped yet. - PM Console/Rollouts: confirm Console references use the current naming (“error budget remaining”, “burn rate”) and avoid promising specific UI until MVP lands. - Support/Docs: confirm the escalation guidance matches current Support process and doesn’t create a new paging expectation. Rollout / comms: After merge, I’ll post a short note in #announcements with links to the new landing page + where to find the runbooks, per ENG-2417 rollout plan. No product behavior changes.
commits: docs: add reliability landing page for tiered SLOs + error budgets
docs: update Hosted API reliability language (SLIs, exclusions, streaming metrics)
docs: update Dedicated reliability expectations (readiness, isolation, fallbacks)
docs: add runbook + comms guideline references throughout
docs: cleanup legacy availability phrasing + broken links
notable_diff_snippets: Before: "Redwood Hosted API is designed to provide 99.99%+ availability." After: "Hosted API reliability targets are defined by tier-specific SLOs measured over a rolling 28-day window. See: Tiered SLO definitions (Hosted vs Dedicated) and SLI exclusions."

Added streaming section: "Latency SLIs for streaming are tracked as (a) time-to-first-token (TTFT) and (b) end-to-end stream duration. Disconnects are tracked separately as streaming disconnect rate; client aborts are excluded per SLI spec."

Dedicated section now calls out readiness: "Dedicated includes a pool readiness SLI (scheduler health + capacity signal). If readiness is degraded, new allocations/scale-out may be delayed even if serving for existing capacity remains within SLO."
conversation: Sean Gallagher (SRE Director): Can you add one more explicit callout that error budget enforcement starts as warn-only for most services and isn’t universal yet? We don’t want teams to think every deploy is blocked automatically today.
Elliot Price (author): Yep. Added a paragraph under “Error budget policy in practice” clarifying warn-only vs soft-block/hard-block and linking to the enforcement playbook page (internal).

Aisha Bello (SRE): In the Hosted streaming section, please ensure we don’t imply that a disconnect is always server fault. The SLI spec explicitly excludes client aborts and certain downstream cancellations; can you link the taxonomy and use “server-side disconnect” phrasing where applicable?

Elliot Price (author): Updated. Now says “streaming disconnect rate (server-side)” and links to the disconnect taxonomy page. Also adjusted the FAQ answer for Support to mention common client abort patterns and what to check.

Marissa Cole (PM, Console & Rollouts): The Console doc mentions “burn forecasts” which is fine, but can you mark it as “MVP: remaining + burn rate; Future: forecast” to avoid confusion with current UI scope?
Elliot Price (author): Done—split into MVP vs Future subsections and added a note that forecasts are not guaranteed for all scopes until we finish backfill + calibration.
Wei Chen (Hosted API reliability docs): Small nit: can we standardize on “timeouts” vs “client timeouts”? In a couple places it reads like we count client-side timeouts as failures, which we don’t.
Elliot Price (author): Fixed those instances to “server-side timeouts” and added a short bullet list of common exclusions with the canonical link.

Kira Thompson (Dedicated/Private operator docs): Please add one sentence that Private deployments are guidance-only right now (no enforced gates by Redwood) since customers manage their own env. I saw one paragraph that could be read as enforcement applies everywhere.
Elliot Price (author): Added a “Private deployments” callout under the landing page: optional targets + mapping guidance, no automatic enforcement initially.
Sean Gallagher (SRE Director): Approving once CI is green. Thanks for tightening the language—this should reduce escalation churn.
release_notes: Internal-only documentation updates: tier-aware SLO language, explicit SLI exclusions, streaming metric definitions, Dedicated readiness notes, and runbook/comms references for error budget burn/exhaustion.
